POLITICS:

Sri Lanka's High Court has convicted 15 men for their roles in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings that killed 279 people and injured over 500. The attacks targeted three churches and three luxury hotels during Easter celebrations, marking Sri Lanka's deadliest terrorist incident since its civil war ended in 2009.

The convicted individuals, all from the Muslim minority community, faced over 23,000 charges including murder and terrorism conspiracy. Prosecutors identified one defendant as the mastermind behind the coordinated attacks. Nine others were acquitted, while one defendant died in custody before the trial concluded.

The bombings, inspired by Islamic State, killed 45 foreigners among the victims. Investigators linked the attacks to two Sri Lankan militant groups. Authorities filed 23,270 charges against 24 suspects in 2021, with all alleged bombers dying in the blasts.

Victims' families and Sri Lanka's Catholic Church welcomed the verdict. A survivor described the ruling as long overdue justice. The court has yet to issue sentencing details for the convicted, though all were found guilty under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.

The case highlights systemic intelligence failures, with a parliamentary committee later finding officials ignored repeated warnings about the attacks. Only 15 of the originally charged 25 suspects faced trial, underscoring the complex legal journey to accountability for one of the nation's most tragic events.

article.title: Sri Lanka Easter attacks: Court finds 15 guilty over deadly bombings
